stepNotes.1: Seven browser adapters converge on a shared Playwright runtime, while webfetch and websearch use separate bounded HTTP transports and registry gates.
stepNotes.2: URLs, redirects, queries, page JavaScript, UIDs, upload paths, response bytes, and browser-produced logs define distinct trust and failure boundaries.
stepNotes.3: Manual web redirects and Exa final-event parsing are coherent, but verbose snapshots, post-navigation buffers, returned redirect URLs, and HTTP-upgrade copy diverge from behavior.
stepNotes.4: Browser calls omit network-isolation enforcement, redirects and clicks bypass destination approval, uploads lack file authorization, and latest-page state is process-global.
stepNotes.5: Ring buffers and streamed success-body caps constrain common growth, while failed opens, Exa error bodies, recursive snapshots, and sessionless cleanup remain exposed.
stepNotes.6: Adapter and transport ownership is mostly clear, but the runtime's claimed session lifetime and verbose snapshot contract are unsupported by its singleton state and return type.
stepNotes.7: The recorded empty catch is cleanup-only; the multi-UID evaluate branch instead remains an unproven Locator serialization path hidden behind explicit any casts.
stepNotes.8: Seven focused files passed 61 tests, with important omissions around session separation, browser policy, redirects, uploads, verbose output, buffer resets, and multi-element evaluation.
stepNotes.9: The existing ledger contains one deferred Low item and no Critical entry; focused tests and core typechecking passed, but browser security gaps block clean sign-off.
